references.text: The Spirit of the Lord came upon Gideon, illustrating how God's power comes upon a person—similar to how God's power left Samson in Judges 16:20.
The Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, a parallel to how the Lord left Samson after he broke his Nazirite vow.
Saul realized that the Lord was with David and had left him, similar to how Samson did not know that the Lord had left him.
The Spirit of the Lord began to stir Samson, which contrasts with this verse where the Lord's power has left him.
The Spirit of the Lord came mightily upon Samson and gave him strength, showing the source of his power which is now gone.
The Spirit of the Lord came mightily upon Samson so that the ropes loosened, but now this power has left him.
Sin separates people from God, explaining why the Lord left Samson after his disobedience.
The Lord will leave Israel until they acknowledge their guilt, a pattern seen in Samson's experience.
